name: Fragmented message
description: One SLTP request written as seven separate TCP writes, with cuts placed at the worst possible offsets.

scenarios.name: seven-fragments
scenarios.description: 134 bytes written as 7 fragments. The rule matches on body content, which can only happen if the peer reassembled every fragment into one message.

request.raw:
SLTP/1.0 ECHO
Request-ID: req-frag-1
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 26

{"note":"split me please"}

scenarios.name: byte-at-a-time
scenarios.description: The same request written one byte per TCP write. The pathological case for any parser that assumes a read contains a whole message.
